problem_text:
A logistics company must select packages to load onto a cargo plane. The available shipments are:
* Package 1: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue $108
* Package 2: volume 3 cubic meters, revenue $263
* Package 3: volume 1 cubic meter, revenue $91
* Package 4: volume 7 cubic meters, revenue $93
* Package 5: volume 34 cubic meters, revenue $118
* Package 6: volume 44 cubic meters, revenue $67
* Package 7: volume 44 cubic meters, revenue $72
* Package 8: volume 28 cubic meters, revenue $106
* Package 9: volume 34 cubic meters, revenue $20
* Package 10: volume 11 cubic meters, revenue $203
* Package 11: volume 11 cubic meters, revenue $70
* Package 12: volume 27 cubic meters, revenue $181
* Package 13: volume 33 cubic meters, revenue $125
* Package 14: volume 44 cubic meters, revenue $244
* Package 15: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue $66
* Package 16: volume 8 cubic meters, revenue $111
* Package 17: volume 34 cubic meters, revenue $63
* Package 18: volume 7 cubic meters, revenue $297
* Package 19: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $53
* Package 20: volume 40 cubic meters, revenue $50
* Package 21: volume 1 cubic meter, revenue $102
* Package 22: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue $244
* Package 23: volume 38 cubic meters, revenue $278
* Package 24: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue $168
* Package 25: volume 43 cubic meters, revenue $160
* Package 26: volume 37 cubic meters, revenue $299

The aircraft's cargo hold has a maximum capacity of 427 cubic meters. Choose the set of packages that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each package must be either fully accepted or rejected.
